question_text:
Arrange these Filipino surnames with Spanish prefixes in correct filing order:
- Dela Cruz, Juan
- Del Rosario, Maria
- De La Torre, Ana
- Delos Santos, Jose

options.text: De La Torre, Ana; Del Rosario, Maria; Dela Cruz, Juan; Delos Santos, Jose
Dela Cruz, Juan; Delos Santos, Jose; Del Rosario, Maria; De La Torre, Ana
Dela Cruz, Juan; De La Torre, Ana; Del Rosario, Maria; Delos Santos, Jose
Delos Santos, Jose; Dela Cruz, Juan; Del Rosario, Maria; De La Torre, Ana

hint_ladder.title: Hint 1
hint_ladder.text: This is all about how we treat those Spanish prefixes like 'Dela,' 'De La,' 'Del,' and 'Delos.' The key is to think of them as part of the surname itself, not as separate words.

hint_ladder.title: Hint 2
hint_ladder.text: Here's the simple rule: when filing, ignore the spaces and the capitalization of the prefix. Treat the entire thing as one continuous word. So 'De La Torre' becomes 'DeLaTorre,' and 'Dela Cruz' becomes 'DelaCruz.'

hint_ladder.title: Hint 3
hint_ladder.text: Now, write all four surnames as one continuous string: DelaCruz, DeLaTorre, DelRosario, DelosSantos. Your job is to sort these alphabetically, letter by letter, as if they were any other word. Which one would come first in a dictionary?

hint_ladder.title: Hint 4
hint_ladder.text: Compare 'DelaCruz' and 'DeLaTorre.' They start the same: D-e-l. The fourth letter is 'a' for both. So we go to the fifth letter: 'C' in DelaCruz and 'T' in DeLaTorre. Since 'C' comes before 'T', Dela Cruz comes first. Now compare 'DelRosario' and 'DelosSantos.' They start D-e-l. The fourth letter is 'R' in DelRosario and 'o' in DelosSantos. 'R' comes before 'o', so Del Rosario comes before Delos Santos. Put it all together.

A.text: This order puts 'De La Torre' first, but that's not quite right. When we compare 'DelaCruz' and 'DeLaTorre' as single strings, they tie on the first four letters (D-e-l-a). The tiebreaker is the fifth letter: 'C' from Cruz versus 'T' from Torre. Since 'C' comes before 'T', 'Dela Cruz' should actually be filed before 'De La Torre.'

B.text: This order has 'Delos Santos' before 'Del Rosario,' which is a common mix-up. When you compare 'DelosSantos' and 'DelRosario' as single strings, the first three letters (D-e-l) are the same. The fourth letter is 'o' for DelosSantos and 'R' for DelRosario. Since 'R' comes before 'o' in the alphabet, 'Del Rosario' should actually come first.

C.text: This is the correct filing order. By treating each prefix as part of the surname and comparing the strings letter by letter, we get: DelaCruz (D-e-l-a-C...) comes before DeLaTorre (D-e-l-a-T...), and DelRosario (D-e-l-R...) comes before DelosSantos (D-e-l-o...).

D.text: This order starts with 'Delos Santos,' but that's not the first name alphabetically. 'Dela Cruz' should be first because 'Dela' comes before 'Delos' when compared letter by letter (the fourth letter 'a' is before 'o'). This looks like the names were sorted in reverse order.
